subject.title: config: use datetime suffix for config backup files instead of numeric rotation

question: Should timestamped config-backup migration preserve or convert existing numbered `.bak.N` recovery points, or may the new cleanup delete them during the first post-upgrade config write?
rationale: Config backups may be the user's only rollback path, and the current branch makes a compatibility-sensitive deletion choice that should not be implicit.

options.title: Preserve Or Convert Legacy Backups
options.body: Require the PR or a replacement to keep existing `.bak.N` files until they are converted into the timestamped retention set or age out safely.

options.title: Accept Timestamp-Only Cleanup
options.body: Allow the migration to delete existing numbered backups, but require explicit maintainer rationale, docs, and proof that the recovery tradeoff is intentional.

options.title: Pause This Branch
options.body: Keep the canonical issue open and close or replace this stale branch if the contributor does not provide proof and the migration-safe repair.

recommendation.title: Preserve Or Convert Legacy Backups
recommendation.body: Require the PR or a replacement to keep existing `.bak.N` files until they are converted into the timestamped retention set or age out safely.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete merged the backup hardening work and has the strongest recent config backup/recovery history among the likely owners.
